title: Revision Techniques
content_html:
Revision Techniques

Evidence-based strategies tailored to GCSE Economics. Economics rewards students who can recall precise definitions — price elasticity formulae, the four factors of production, the difference between monetary and fiscal policy — and apply that knowledge to unfamiliar contexts. Paper 1 covers microeconomics; Paper 2 covers macroeconomics. Both papers end with 9- and 12-mark evaluation questions where the ability to analyse chains of reasoning and weigh competing factors separates good answers from excellent ones. Use the strategies below to build rock-solid recall and analytical confidence across both papers.

Foundation Techniques

Start early — use these from day one
Active recall

Retrieval Practice

Test yourself on definitions, formulae, and diagrams rather than re-reading. Brain dumps on “market failure” or “government objectives” reveal exactly what you don’t know — and strengthen what you do.

 Distributed practice

Spaced Repetition

Revisit the same material at 1, 3, 7, 14, 30-day gaps. Concepts like PED, income elasticity, and the multiplier need spacing to stick. Works better than cramming every time.

 Deep thinking

Elaborative Interrogation

Ask “why?” and “how?” to deepen understanding. Why does a rise in interest rates reduce consumer spending? How does a negative externality cause market failure? Turn memorised facts into understood economic chains.

Consolidation Techniques

Use these once you know the basics
Visual learning

Dual Coding

Combine words and visuals. Annotated demand and supply diagrams, production possibility frontiers, and the economic cycle stick far better than text alone — and Economics is a highly diagram-driven subject.

 Mixed practice

Interleaving

Mix microeconomics and macroeconomics topics in one session. Trains you to identify whether a question is testing markets, elasticity, inflation, unemployment, or trade — the discrimination skill the exam tests hardest.

 Structured notes

Knowledge Organisers

One page per topic. Key definitions, formulae, diagram sketches, and policy examples. Redraw from memory. The base layer of every solid Economics revision routine.

Exam Preparation

Final weeks — sharpen and apply
Exam conditions

Timed Practice

Simulate the real thing. Economics papers mix short-answer recall with extended 9- and 12-mark evaluations — practising under time pressure builds the judgement to deploy analysis and evaluation confidently.
